summary: Umpqua NF lookout built by the CCC in 1933 on Rattlesnake Mountain; destroyed in the October 1962 Columbus Day storm. No source describes the site today.

facts.design: 30-foot round hemlock timber pole tower with a 14x14 hip-roofed L-4 cab
facts.status_note: Destroyed by the October 1962 Columbus Day storm; no source describes what remains on the summit.
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Umpqua National Forest

access.note: Summit is reached on foot by trails through the Rogue-Umpqua Divide Wilderness, starting from Forest Road 870. Based on a 2015 hike report; no closure found, but current conditions are unverified.

visit.trail_note: 2015 hike report: start at Happy Camp near the end of Forest Road 870; trail #1497 leads to the summit

events.note: Built by the Civilian Conservation Corps as a 30-foot round hemlock tower with a 14x14 L-4 cab
A lookout was on duty in September 1937 when a ranger and a writer passed on a trail below the summit
After a lightning storm the lookout later found fire in an old stump below the summit; he had seen no smoke earlier
Destroyed by the October 12, 1962 Columbus Day storm

evidence.quote: Built in 1933, this 30' pole L-4 tower was destroyed in the 1962 Columbus Day hurricane.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register, firelookout.com and the 2015 hike report call the 1962 storm a hurricane; the Oregon lookouts history calls it the Columbus Day storm. These are the same event.

notes_for_editor: The 1933 build and 1962 destruction agree across four sources. Access comes from a 2015 hike report, so the public level and trail note are provisional until someone checks current conditions. No source describes remains on the summit. No new photo with a usable URL was found. The brief's access 'unknown' is superseded by the trail description.
